Bug at line 8: `currentTime > expiry` rejects the token at the exact boundary when it should still be valid. Token expires *after* the expiry timestamp, not *at* it.

Fix:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="edit">
<parameter name="path">/tmp/chisle-ablate-work-vgAXU7/auth_middleware.py</parameter>
<parameter name="edits">[{"line": 8, "old": "    if currentTime > expiry:", "new": "    if currentTime >= expiry:"}]</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Done. The boundary condition was backwards: `>` (strictly greater) means the token is valid up to and including the expiry time, but then rejected at that exact moment. Using `>=` (greater or equal) is standard for token expiry: if current time equals or passes the expiry timestamp, the token is expired. This aligns with how most token systems work—a token valid until 10:00:00 should be rejected at 10:00:00, not 10:00:01.
